title: “Amor” by Nat King Cole
text: "L-O-V-E" is a song written by Bert Kaempfert and Milt Gabler, recorded by Nat King Cole for his 1965 studio album L-O-V-E.

title: “Nosotros/Piel Canela” by Eydie Gormé & Los Panchos/Chico Miranda
text: Eydie Gormé was an American singer who achieved notable success in pop, Latin, and jazz genres. She sang solo and in the duo Steve and Eydie with her husband, Steve Lawrence, on albums and television.
listen: Nosotros/Piel Canela Eydie Gormé & Los Panchos/Chico Miranda

title: “Do Re Mi” by The Cousins/Millie Small/Simonette
text: Millicent Dolly May Small CD was a Jamaican singer who is best known for her international hit "My Boy Lollipop" (1964). The song reached number two in both the UK and US charts and sold over seven million copies worldwide.
listen: Do Re Mi The Cousins/Millie Small/Simonette

title: “Es una mujer (She's a Woman)/Me siento bien (I Feel Fine)” by The Beatles/Juan Ramón
text: "She's a Woman" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written primarily by Paul McCartney and credited to Lennon–McCartney. It was released on a non-album single in November 1964 as the B-side to "I Feel Fine", except in North America, where it also appeared on the album Beatles '65, released in December 1964.
listen: Es una mujer (She's a Woman)/Me siento bien (I Feel Fine) The Beatles/Juan Ramón

title: “Ma vie” by Alain Barriere
text: Alain Barrière was a French singer, who was active from the 1950s until his death and was known for participating in the Eurovision Song Contest 1963.

title: “Amor, perdóname (Amore scusami)” by John Foster/Juan Ramón/ Tito Rodríguez/Dalida/Claudia
text: Paolo Occhipinti, best known as John Foster, is an Italian former singer and journalist.
listen: Amor, perdóname (Amore scusami) John Foster/Juan Ramón/ Tito Rodríguez/Dalida/Claudia

title: “He comprendido que te amo (Ho capito che ti amo)” by Luigi Tenco/Wilma Goich/José Antonio
text: Luigi Tenco was an Italian singer-songwriter. He died on the night of 27 January 1967 after a performance at the Sanremo Music Festival.
listen: He comprendido que te amo (Ho capito che ti amo) Luigi Tenco/Wilma Goich/José Antonio

title: “Venecia sin ti” by Charles Aznavour/Juan Ramón
text: "Que c'est triste Venise" is a song written by Armenian-French artist Charles Aznavour and Françoise Dorin and sung by Aznavour about Venice. It was first recorded in French by Aznavour in 1964, and later in Spanish ("Venecia sin ti"), German ("Venedig im Grau"), English ("How Sad Venice Can Be" or "Venice Blue" cover of Bobby Darin), and most notably in 1971 in Italian ("Com'è triste Venezia").
listen: Venecia sin ti Charles Aznavour/Juan Ramón

title: “¡Socorro! (Help!)” by The Beatles/Los Búhos
text: "Help!" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles that served as the title song for the 1965 film and the band's accompanying soundtrack album. It was released as a single in July 1965, and was number one for three weeks in the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: “Shame and Scandal in the Family” by Shawn Elliot/Sacha Distel/Lance Percival/ Juan Montego & The Kingston Orchestra
text: "Shame and Scandal in the Family", also known as "Shame & Scandal" for short, is a song written by calypso singer Sir Lancelot for the film I Walked with a Zombie in 1943 and originally titled "Fort Holland Calypso Song". Sir Lancelot issued his recording of it in the late 1940s.
wiki: Shame and Scandal in the Family
listen: Shame and Scandal in the Family Shawn Elliot/Sacha Distel/Lance Percival/ Juan Montego & The Kingston Orchestra

title: “A veces me pregunto yo” by Richard Anthony
text: Richard Anthony was an Egyptian-born French pop singer who had his greatest success in the 1960s and 1970s.
listen: A veces me pregunto yo Richard Anthony

title: “Changuito Dios” by Palito Ortega
text: Ramón Bautista Ortega is an Argentine singer and actor, better known as Palito Ortega (pronounced ). Ortega is an icon of Argentine popular music, and is considered one of the main representatives of the musical style called New wave that marked the Hispanic-American music between the years '60 and '70.

title: Ranger 8 crashes into the Moon after a successful mission of photographing possible landing sites for the Apollo program astronauts.
text: Ranger 8 was a lunar probe in the Ranger program, a robotic spacecraft series launched by NASA in the early-to-mid-1960s to obtain the first close-up images of the Moon's surface. These pictures helped select landing sites for Apollo missions and were used for scientific study.

title: NASA launches Gemini 3, the United States' first two-person space flight (crew: Gus Grissom and John Young).
text: Gemini 3 was the first crewed mission in NASA's Project Gemini and was the first time two American astronauts flew together into space. On March 23, 1965, astronauts Gus Grissom and John Young flew three low Earth orbits in their spacecraft, which they nicknamed Molly Brown.

title: NASA launches Gemini 5 (Gordon Cooper, Pete Conrad) on the first 1-week space flight, as well as the first test of fuel cells for electrical power on such a mission.
text: Gemini 5 was a 1965 crewed spaceflight in NASA's Project Gemini. It was the third crewed Gemini flight, the eleventh crewed American spaceflight (including two X-15 flights above 100 kilometers (54 nmi)), and the nineteenth human spaceflight.

title: Venera program: The Soviet Union launches the Venera 3 space probe from Baikonur, Kazakhstan toward Venus. (On March 1, 1966, it becomes the first spacecraft to reach the surface of another planet).
text: The Venera program was a series of space probes developed by the Soviet Union between 1961 and 1984 to gather information about the planet Venus. A total of eighteen probes were sent, including two related Vega probes.

title: At the Hammaguira launch facility in the Sahara Desert, France launches a Diamant-A rocket with its first satellite, Astérix-1 on board, becoming the third country to enter space.
text: The Sahara is a desert spanning North Africa. With an area of 9,200,000 square kilometres (3,600,000 sq mi), it is the largest hot desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall, smaller only than the deserts of Antarctica and the northern Arctic.

title: Discovery of NML Cygni, a red hypergiant and the largest star known, at about 1,650 times the Sun's radius.
text: NML Cygni or V1489 Cygni is a red hypergiant or red supergiant (RHG or RSG) in the constellation Cygnus. It is one of the largest known stars, and is also one of the most luminous and massive cool hypergiants, as well as one of the most luminous stars in the Milky Way.

title: Soviet fiction writers Yuli Daniel and Andrei Sinyavsky are sentenced to five and seven years, respectively, for "anti-Soviet" writings.
text: Andrei Donatovich Sinyavsky was a Russian writer and Soviet dissident known as a defendant in the Sinyavsky–Daniel trial of 1965. Sinyavsky was a literary critic for Novy Mir and wrote works critical of Soviet society under the pseudonym Abram Tertz (Абрам Терц) published in the West to avoid censorship in the Soviet Union.

title: While Soviet author and translator Valery Tarsis is abroad, the Soviet Union negates his citizenship.
text: Valery Yakovlevich Tarsis was a Ukrainian writer, literary critic, and translator. He was highly critical of the communist regime.

title: Harold Pinter's play The Homecoming receives its world première at the New Theatre, Cardiff, from the Royal Shakespeare Company under Peter Hall. Its London première follows on June 3 at the Aldwych Theatre, with Vivien Merchant, Pinter's…
text: Harold Pinter was an English playwright, screenwriter, director and actor. A recipient of the 2005 Nobel Prize in Literature, Pinter was one of the most influential modern dramatists of British theatre with a writing career that spanned more than 50 years.

title: The world première of A High Wind in Jamaica, a film from Richard Hughes's 1929 novel, featuring the future novelist Martin Amis, son of Kingsley Amis, as a teenage actor.
text: Sir Martin Louis Amis was an English novelist, essayist, memoirist, screenwriter and critic. He is best known for his novels Money (1984) and London Fields (1989).

title: International Poetry Incarnation, a performance poetry event, takes place at London's Royal Albert Hall before an audience of 7,000, with members of the Beat Generation featuring. Adrian Mitchell reads "To Whom It May Concern".
text: Performance poetry is poetry that is specifically composed for or during a performance before an audience. It covers a variety of styles and genres.

title: The London première of Frank Marcus' farce The Killing of Sister George (at the Duke of York's Theatre) is among the first mainstream British plays with lesbian characters. Beryl Reid plays the title rôle. It has been previewed in April at…
text: The Tom Stoppard Theatre is a West End theatre in St Martin's Lane, in the City of Westminster, London.

title: J. D. Salinger's novella "Hapworth 16, 1924" takes up most of an issue of The New Yorker magazine dated today. It will be the last of his works published before his death in 2010.
text: Jerome David Salinger was an American writer best known for his 1951 novel The Catcher in the Rye. Salinger published several short stories in Story magazine in 1940, before serving in World War II. In 1948, his critically acclaimed story "A Perfect Day for Bananafish" appeared in The New Yorker, which published much of his later work.

title: The English novelists Kingsley Amis and Elizabeth Jane Howard marry at Marylebone register office in London, as his second marriage and her third.
text: Sir Kingsley William Amis was an English novelist, poet, critic and teacher. He wrote more than 20 novels, six volumes of poetry, a memoir, short stories, radio and television scripts, and works of social and literary criticism.

title: A record price of 760,000 guineas is paid at Christie's London auction house for Rembrandt's painting Titus.
text: The guinea was a coin, minted in Great Britain between 1663 and 1814, that contained approximately one-quarter troy ounce (7.8 g) of gold.

title: Avant-garde artists Marta Minujín and Rubén Santantonín present La Menesunda in Buenos Aires, one of the first installations in art history.
text: Marta Minujín is an Argentine conceptual and performance artist.

title: Indica Gallery counterculture bookshop and art gallery opens in London.
text: The Indica Gallery was a counterculture art gallery in Mason's Yard, St James's, London from 1965 to 1967, in the basement of the Indica Bookshop. John Dunbar, Peter Asher, and Barry Miles owned it, and Paul McCartney supported it and hosted a show of Yoko Ono's work in November 1966, at which Ono met John Lennon.

title: Release in the United States of the biographical film The Agony and the Ecstasy with Charlton Heston portraying Michelangelo.
text: Charlton Heston was an American actor and political activist. He gained stardom for his leading man roles in numerous Hollywood films including biblical epics, historical drama films, science-fiction films, and action films.
